title: Raus! Raus! Raus!: the Judge's Son, the Mount of Truth, and the Attic in Munich
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Kronstadt, birth in the judge's house
stops.date_confidence: attested. Date and parentage from de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'; the Council Square coordinate is the town centre pin, not a documented address, since no source located in this pass names the house.
stops.campa: In Kronstadt, at the Transylvanian foot of the Carpathians, a son is born to Carl Samuel Gräser, district judge and senator, and to Charlotte Gräser born Pelzer. The family is Saxon, Protestant, respectable in exactly the way a judge's household is respectable: offices, books, a surname that carries across the town square. Nothing in the record of that February morning marks it out from any other birth in the town's Protestant families that winter. The date entered is the sixteenth, the year 1879, and the child is registered as Gustav Arthur.
suggested_refs: The Lutheran parish registers of Kronstadt (Brasov) for February 1879
Hans Bergel's Transylvanian-perspective account of the Gräser family (2009)

stops.name: Kronstadt, the gymnasium abandoned
stops.date_confidence: attested that he left the gymnasium at fifteen (de.wikipedia: 'Im Alter von 15 Jahren ging Gustav Gräser vom Gymnasium ab'), which places it in 1894. The school is NOT named by that source: the Brukenthal Gymnasium at Hermannstadt is gusto-graeser.info circle tradition [R] and the stop is therefore pinned at Kronstadt, not Hermannstadt. His father's death in the same year is documented separately and is the likelier proximate cause; no source states the two together.
stops.campa: At fifteen he walks out of the gymnasium and does not go back. The same year his father dies, and the house that was built on a judge's salary and a judge's standing stops being either. No source states that the two events were connected, and none separates them. He tries his hands instead: metalwork, goldsmithing, carving, the trades where a boy learns by cutting into a material until it yields. Which school it was nobody records. The German account gives his age and nothing else.
suggested_refs: gusto-graeser.info chronology, which names the Brukenthal Gymnasium at Hermannstadt and is the only carrier of that detail
sources: de.wikipedia.org, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)', for the father's death in 1894

stops.name: Budapest, the medal at the Millennium Exhibition
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the prize (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'), often reported specifically as a gold medal. The month is set to the exhibition's opening season; no source found gives a date of award. The coordinate is the Varosliget exhibition ground.
stops.campa: Hungary keeps its thousandth year with an exhibition in the Varosliget, pavilions thrown up across the park to show the kingdom what the kingdom has made. Among the carved work a piece by the seventeen-year-old from Kronstadt takes a prize, reported ever after as gold; no source located names the carving, its material or its subject. It is the last moment at which Gustav Gräser is entirely legible to the institutions around him: a promising applied artist, medalled by a state exhibition, with the decorative trades open in front of him.
suggested_refs: The 1896 Budapest Millennium Exhibition catalogues and prize lists, Varosliget

stops.name: Vienna, the years of art study
stops.date_confidence: attested only as 'Seit 1897 studierte er Kunst in Wien' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). The Kunstgewerbeschule is NOT in that source and is [R]; the coordinate given here is the Stubenring building of the school as it now stands, and should be read as the traditional location rather than a documented one.
stops.campa: From 1897 he is in Vienna studying art, in the capital at the moment the Secession is being declared and the whole apparatus of decorative craft is being argued over by men his own age. The record of these years is thin: a city, a discipline, a start date. Seit 1897 studierte er Kunst in Wien, says the German article, and then stops. Which school, under whom, for how long, and whether he finished are all blank. Within a year he is living in a commune on the western edge of the same city.
suggested_refs: Enrolment records of the k.k. Kunstgewerbeschule, Vienna, 1897-1898, which would settle whether he studied there

stops.name: Himmelhof, inside Diefenbach's Humanitas
stops.date_confidence: attested that he joined and left Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach's Humanitas commune at the Himmelhof in Ober-St-Veit (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'; en.wikipedia, 'Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach'), which housed up to twenty-four members 1897-99. The coordinate is approximate: the exact address of the former guesthouse was not confirmed in this pass. The Guttzeit-Losert-Diefenbach ideological genealogy could not be verified and is [R].
stops.campa: At the old guesthouse called Auf dem Himmeln, above Ober-St-Veit, the painter Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach keeps a community of two dozen: long hair, sandals, reform dress, no meat, no property, art practiced as a way of living rather than a way of earning. The Humanitas runs from 1897 to 1899 and Gräser is inside it for part of that. He takes all of it, and the prophetic posture with it, the beard, the tunic. What he refuses is the one condition Diefenbach attaches to everything else, which is obedience. He is out within months.
suggested_refs: The 2015 exhibition 'Künstler und Propheten. Eine geheime Geschichte der Moderne 1872-1972', Schirn Kunsthalle Frankfurt, which set Gräser in a prophet-artist lineage running from Diefenbach

stops.name: Transylvania, the paintings burned and the one kept
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R] for the scene. The vision of an angel with a sword and the destruction of nearly all his canvases are Hermann Müller's narrative (Der Dichter und sein Guru, 2nd ed. 1979), advocacy scholarship by the man who later rescued and edited the estate, and are not independently verifiable. What IS attested (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser') is that Der Liebe Macht was made in a few weeks after 1898 and that it survives; that it was painted in Transylvania is Müller's placing, not the sourced statement. The break with the family is dated 1899 in the same article. Month arbitrary, set to order the segment.
stops.campa: He turns back east toward the country he was born in, and there, according to the account his later circle keeps, an angel with a sword stands over him and orders him out into the world. He destroys nearly every canvas he has made. In 1899 he breaks with the family altogether and starts walking. One picture survives the burning: Der Liebe Macht, a naked couple walking out of a burning industrial landscape toward animals, water and each other, the Fall run backwards. That it was painted in Transylvania is Müller's placing, not the record's.
suggested_refs: Der Liebe Macht, now held at the Museo Casa Anatta on Monte Verità above Ascona
Hermann Müller, Der Dichter und sein Guru (2nd ed. 1979), the sole source for the vision and the burning
sources: Hermann Müller, Der Dichter und sein Guru (2nd ed. 1979) [R]

segments.name: Ohne Zwang: the Brothers and the Mount of Truth

stops.name: Przemysl, the association without coercion
stops.date_confidence: contradiction, flagged not resolved. The operator tradition has Gusto running a land commune called Ohne Zwang in Galicia with his brother. de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)' instead documents a Verein named 'Ohne Zwang' founded in the Przemysl garrison by Karl Gräser as Geschäftsführer with the former Archduke Leopold Ferdinand (Leopold Wölfling) as president, during Karl's service 1894-1901: an association, not a commune, and Gusto's participation is NOT attested there. What is undisputed is that Gusto signed poems O.Z. for years afterward. The pin is the Przemysl garrison; the earlier placeholder at 49.8/24.0 was ninety kilometres wrong.
stops.campa: In the Galician garrison town of Przemysl, his older brother Karl, a career officer of the k.u.k. infantry, founds an association with a former Habsburg archduke who has given up his rank: they call it Ohne Zwang, Without Coercion. The president is Leopold Wölfling, born Archduke Leopold Ferdinand; Karl runs it as Geschäftsführer while still serving in Infanterieregiment Nr. 58. Whether Gusto is in Przemysl at all is not recorded anywhere this pass could reach. What is recorded is that for years afterward he signs his poems O.Z.
stops.quote_source: Name of the Verein founded at the Przemysl garrison by Karl Gräser with Leopold Wölfling, per de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'
suggested_refs: The k.u.k. Infanterieregiment Nr. 58 records for the Przemysl garrison, 1894-1901
Gräser's poems signed O.Z., collected in the posthumous editions
sources: gusto-graeser.info circle tradition, for Gusto's participation [R]

stops.name: Munich, the founding meeting
stops.date_confidence: attested. The group constitutes itself in Munich-Schwabing in October 1900 (de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'), the coordinate inherited byte-identical from ida_hoffmann.journey.json, which carries the same stop at the same date and names Gusto Gräser among those present. Day of month set to 01.
stops.campa: In Schwabing the plan finally assembles a set of people around itself. Henri Oedenkoven, the industrialist's son; Ida Hofmann, the piano teacher who will write its manifestos; her sister Jenny; Lotte Hattemer; Karl Gräser, out of the army; and Karl's younger brother, twenty-one years old, already dressed as what he intends to remain. They mean to buy land in the south and start a cooperative colony on it, with no meat, no property and no coercion. It is October 1900. None of them has seen the land yet.
suggested_refs: Ida Hofmann's own published accounts of the colony's founding
sources: ida_hoffmann.journey.json (Colegio Invisible corpus, same stop, date and coordinate)

stops.name: Monte Monescia, the hill bought from Pioda
stops.date_confidence: attested that four hectares on Monte Monescia above Ascona were bought from Alfredo Pioda in the autumn of 1900, the group travelling south via Oberammergau and Cadenabbia (de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'; ida_hoffmann.journey.json). The name Monte Verità does NOT date from the purchase: both Wikipedia articles state it first appears in the 1902 sanatorium prospectus. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus pin used across laban, ida_hoffmann, mary_wigman and suzanne_perrottet; note it sits some 370 m from the Casa Anatta coordinate given in de.wikipedia, 'Casa Anatta', an unresolved disagreement.
stops.campa: They come down through Oberammergau and Cadenabbia to the Lago Maggiore and buy four hectares of hillside above Ascona from Alfredo Pioda, a Ticinese who had once wanted a theosophical lay monastery on the same slope. The hill is called Monte Monescia. Nobody calls it the Mount of Truth yet; that name is printed for the first time two years later, on a prospectus offering rooms to paying guests. For now there is terraced ground, chestnut trees and a view south over the lake.
suggested_refs: Alfredo Pioda's earlier theosophical project for the same slope
The 1902 sanatorium prospectus, in which the name Monte Verità first appears

stops.name: Monte Verità, the light-air huts
stops.date_confidence: attested. Light-air huts from January 1901 per ida_hoffmann.journey.json, corroborated in outline by de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus pin. The word vegan is anachronistic for the period and is avoided; the sources describe a diet without animal products.
stops.campa: The huts go up in January: light and air let through the walls on principle, sun on the skin as medicine, a diet with no animal in it anywhere, reform clothing or none, cooperative accounts, schooling for children that is not schooling as anyone present remembers it, and women who own their own decisions. It is not a nudist colony and it is not a sanatorium, though it will be called both. What is being attempted is the rebuilding of the whole human organism at once, from first principles, in wooden huts, in a Ticinese January.
suggested_refs: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verità: Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906)

stops.name: Monte Verità, the youngest founder put out
stops.date_confidence: contradiction, flagged not resolved. ida_hoffmann.journey.json dates the expulsion June 1901 and this file inherits its date and coordinate; no external source located in this pass gives a month, and the nearest documented anchor is Karl Gräser's departure from the community in December 1901 (de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)'). That he is no longer a normal member by 1901-02 is attested [A]. The pure-prophet-against-the-capitalist framing is his own later circle's [R]: disputes over labour and his refusal to subordinate himself to communal organisation are also on the record.
stops.campa: Within a year the colony has guests, fees and accounts, because Oedenkoven intends it to survive by paying for itself, and the youngest of its founders will not have any of the three. He is put out, or withdraws, depending on who is telling it. By February 1901 he is not a normal member of it. He does not leave the mountain either. He goes down the slope to a rock grotto below the meadow and stays there, close enough that every visitor to the sanatorium for the next decade will be told there is a prophet living in the rocks underneath it.
suggested_refs: Henri Oedenkoven's sanatorium accounts and prospectuses for Monte Verità

stops.name: Above Ascona, Karl and Jenny on adjoining ground
stops.date_confidence: contradiction, flagged not resolved. Date and coordinate inherited from ida_hoffmann.journey.json, which places the second household in September 1901 and flags its own coordinate as reconstructed. de.wikipedia, 'Karl Gräser (Offizier)' instead dates Karl's departure from the community to December 1901. Karl and Jenny Hofmann lived in free marriage in the 'Gräser-Haus' on a moneyless regime; Karl fell ill in 1915, married Jenny on 28 September 1916 and died on 28 October 1916 in Kassel, not in Ascona.
stops.campa: The split takes a second couple with it. Karl Gräser, the former officer, and Jenny Hofmann, Ida's own sister, set up their own household on ground a few hundred metres from the sanatorium and from Gusto's grotto: no money kept in the house at all, no marriage on paper, the doctrine held harder than the institution holds it. Three settlements now share the slope, within shouting distance, practicing versions of one belief that none of them will reconcile with the others. None of the three moves away.
suggested_refs: The Gräser-Haus above Ascona, which later housed Ascona's first picture gallery

stops.name: Vienna, the imprint of Efeublätter
stops.date_confidence: the book is attested as Efeublätter, Vienna 1902 (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser', works list); no text of it was retrievable in this pass. The stop is placed at the imprint city, and NO source located here documents Gräser's own presence in Vienna in 1902. Separately, the claim that he refused Austrian military service around 1902 and served about a year in prison is operator tradition [R] with no place attached and no corroborating source found; it is recorded here because dropping it silently would lose it.
stops.campa: His first book carries a Vienna imprint and the date 1902: Efeublätter, ivy leaves, poems. Not one line of it could be recovered in this pass, only the title and the year, which is roughly the condition of most of what he wrote. He publishes in the way a man with no publisher publishes, in small self-made runs handed to whoever is standing there. Somewhere in the same stretch of years, by an account his circle carries and no document confirms, the Austrian army calls him, he refuses, and he serves about a year in prison. No place is attached to that year.
suggested_refs: Efeublätter (Vienna, 1902), of which no copy was located in this pass
sources: operator brief, for the 1902 military refusal and imprisonment [R]

stops.name: Arcegno, the cave from the municipality of Losone
stops.date_confidence: attested that from 1903 the municipality of Losone gave him a cave and a forest meadow near Arcegno (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Coordinate supplied by the operator brief. Note the disagreement: the corpus files (ida_hoffmann, laban, mary_wigman, suzanne_perrottet) locate 'Gräser's grotto' below the Monte Verità meadow at 46.1608/8.7658, roughly 2.5 km east of this Arcegno point. The sources may be describing two different rock shelters or one imprecisely; not resolved here.
stops.campa: The commune of Losone makes him a gift that suits nobody else: a cave in the woods above Arcegno and the meadow in front of it. He takes it and lives there on and off for years, on roots, nuts, fruit and berries by every account that survives, nearly naked, with a fire. Unlike Diefenbach he collects nobody who is required to obey him; people come up, look at him, and walk back down. Hair, beard, tunic, headband, sandals, rock. Visitors reach for Diogenes, for John the Baptist, for Francis, for Zarathustra.
suggested_refs: The Pagangrotte above Arcegno, in the commune of Losone
sources: operator brief, for the cave coordinate

stops.name: Arcegno woods, the moonlight dances
stops.date_confidence: attested that moonlight dances took place in the Arcegno woods, that local followers were called balabiott, and that contemporaries compared the movement to dervish dance (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). The year 1905 is approximate and set to order the segment. The claim that Gräser founded modern dance is an overclaim and is rejected here: the institutional line runs through Rudolf von Laban's school from 1913 and through Mary Wigman.
stops.campa: On clear nights they dance in the woods above Arcegno, in the moonlight, without clothes, and the valley below names them balabiott, the naked dancers. People who watched described something religious rather than something choreographic, and reached for the dervishes to say what it was like. Nothing here is taught, notated or repeated the same way twice. Modern dance does not start in these woods, whatever is claimed later: the notation and the training arrive on this mountain in 1913, with Laban, and run on through Mary Wigman.
suggested_refs: The balabiott of Arcegno, in Ticinese local memory
sources: laban.journey.json and mary_wigman.journey.json, for the institutional dance lineage, cross-checked and not duplicated here

stops.name: Locarno, the exhibition with his brother
stops.date_confidence: attested, dated 1906/07 in the source: '1906/07 machten die Brüder gemeinsam eine Kunstausstellung in Locarno. Aus ihr entstand Asconas erste Gemäldegalerie im Hause von Karl Gräser' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Month set to 01; the year could equally be 1907.
stops.campa: The two brothers, who between them have refused the army, the family and the colony, hang an exhibition in Locarno in 1906 or 1907; the sources do not choose between the years. What hung on those walls, and whether any of it sold, no source reached here records. The man from the cave is an exhibiting artist again for a season, eight years after burning most of what he had painted. Out of the exhibition comes the first picture gallery Ascona has ever had, in Karl's own front rooms above the town, in a house that keeps no money in it.
suggested_refs: Ascona's first picture gallery, in the Gräser-Haus

stops.name: Arcegno cave, Hermann Hesse in the rocks
stops.date_confidence: attested that Hermann Hesse, in Ascona in April 1907 for a fasting and primitive-living experiment connected to his story In den Felsen, spent time at Gräser's cave and that they read Eastern texts together, and that the contact affected Hesse deeply (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Coordinate is the operator's Arcegno cave point; hermann_hesse.journey.json carries its own 'Ascona, the mountain of truth' stop for the same visit at 46.1608/8.7658 and does NOT name Gräser, a gap in that file rather than a contradiction of this one. The stronger claim, that Gräser was Hesse's secret guru and IS Demian or the Leo of Journey to the East, is Hermann Müller's thesis [R], not settled fact.
stops.campa: Hermann Hesse comes to Ascona to fast, to sleep on rock, to find out what a man is when the furniture is taken away, and writes a story called In den Felsen out of it. He spends his time at the cave above Arcegno with the man already living there, and they read the Bhagavad Gita and the Tao Te Ching together in the meadow in front of it. Nine years later Hesse writes Demian, and Müller's whole case rests on that. What Hesse himself left on the record is a phrase: der Waldmensch mit dem dritten Auge, the forest man with the third eye.
stops.quote: der Waldmensch mit dem dritten Auge
stops.quote_source: Hermann Hesse's characterization of Gräser, as reported in de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'; no pinpoint to a specific Hesse text is given by that source
suggested_refs: Hermann Hesse, In den Felsen (1907)
Hermann Müller, Der Dichter und sein Guru (2nd ed. 1979), the source of the secret-guru thesis
hermann_hesse.journey.json, whose April 1907 Ascona stop does not currently name Gräser

stops.name: Vienna, Elisabeth Dorr and the birth of Gertrud
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]. The household with Wilhelmine Elisabeth Dorr (also Streng, later Braumann), formed around 1907-08 outside legal marriage, and the birth of Gertrud Gräser in Vienna on 4 April 1910 come from gusto-graeser.info family-reconstruction tradition via the operator brief; the birth date and city are treated as attested within that tradition, the later attribution of two further daughters, Heidi/Grete (b. 1913) and Waldtraud/Lottchen (b. 1916), is unresolved and complicated by Dorr's earlier marriage. The couple separated around 1917-18.
stops.campa: Wilhelmine Elisabeth Dorr enters his life around 1907 and stays roughly a decade, in a household with no legal marriage under it and no fixed address for most of its duration. On the fourth of April 1910 their daughter Gertrud is born in Vienna. The genealogy after that is a thicket: an earlier marriage of Dorr's, surnames that change, two more girls attributed to the household by a family tradition that cannot fully account for them. Heidi, called Grete, is put at 1913; Waldtraud, called Lottchen, at 1916. The couple separate around 1917.
suggested_refs: gusto-graeser.info family reconstruction, the sole carrier of the Dorr household's genealogy
sources: operator brief, per gusto-graeser.info family-reconstruction tradition [R]

segments.name: Raus! Raus! Raus!: the Wagon Years

stops.name: Munich, the siskin-green wagon
stops.date_confidence: attested in detail: '1911 mit Frau und sieben Kindern im selbstgebauten Wohnwagen, auf dem Dach eine hölzerne Schlange, von München nach Berlin', the siskin-green wagon lettered Raus! Raus! Raus! in giant letters (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). The frequently repeated claim that he appeared at Munich's Simplicissimus cabaret from around 1910 is NOT in that article; the attribution is false as cited and is not carried in the prose. Month set to 01.
stops.campa: He builds the wagon himself and puts a carved wooden serpent on the roof of it. The body is painted siskin green and lettered along the side in letters a passer-by cannot fail to read: Raus! Raus! Raus! Out, out, out. Into it go his wife and seven children, and the whole household leaves Munich for Berlin at the speed of a horse, stopping in towns to recite, to talk and to dance for whoever gathers. The year is 1911 and the road runs about six hundred kilometres.
stops.quote_source: Lettering painted on Gräser's self-built wagon, 1911, per de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'
suggested_refs: Gerhart Hauptmann, Der Narr in Christo Emanuel Quint (1910), whose title figure de.wikipedia names Gräser as a model for

stops.name: Berlin, the caravan arrives
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the route Munich to Berlin (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'); no month is given by any source located, and June is set to order the segment. The coordinate is the Berlin city centre pin.
stops.campa: The wagon reaches Berlin, four million people and the loudest capital in Europe, and parks a barefoot Transylvanian and seven children in the middle of it. For the next years this is how the family lives and how he works: arrive, unhitch, speak in the open to whoever stops, hand out printed sheets, move on before the police make it a matter. The sheets were never collected and almost none of them survive. He is not lecturing. He calls what he does conversation, and he does it standing in the street.
suggested_refs: Gräser's self-printed sheets and handouts of the wagon years, largely uncollected

stops.name: Dresden, expelled from Saxony
stops.date_confidence: attested that he was expelled from Saxony in 1912, and that the pamphlets Ein Freund ist da, mach auf! and Heimat date from the same year (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). No month is given; no source names Dresden specifically as the place of the expulsion order, and the Saxon capital pin is used for a kingdom-wide measure.
stops.campa: The Kingdom of Saxony expels him in 1912. The same year two pamphlets appear over his name, Ein Freund ist da, mach auf! and Heimat: a friend is here, open the door, and home. A state that can move an army by rail decides that a man with a horse, a wooden snake and a stack of pamphlets should be outside its borders by a fixed date. No source reached names the month, the office or the ground given, and no copy of either pamphlet was located in this pass. He crosses the border.
suggested_refs: Ein Freund ist da, mach auf! (1912)
Heimat (1912)

stops.name: Karlsruhe, expelled from Baden
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'); no month located, and no source names Karlsruhe as the place of the order. The Baden capital pin stands for a grand-duchy-wide measure.
stops.campa: Baden follows Saxony a year later. Same pattern, different capital: an order signed, a period allowed, a departure across a border into another German state that will get around to the same order in its own time. He does not contest any of them in court, and he is not trying to hold ground. Nobody has produced the Baden file, so the wording of the order, the official who signed it and the reason entered on it are all unknown. What survives is the year: 1913.
suggested_refs: Baden expulsion files, 1913, not located in this pass

stops.name: Stuttgart, the public conversations
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]. The operator brief places public conversations around Stuttgart in 1912-13 drawing young people from the Jugendbewegung milieu; this is consistent with de.wikipedia's account of the wandering-agitator years but is not separately sourced there. Month arbitrary. The Stuttgart city-centre pin is used; the 1929 Vagabundenkongress stop later in this file uses the Killesberg coordinate instead, since that site is documented.
stops.campa: In and around Stuttgart he holds what he insists on calling conversations, not lectures: he stands, people gather, anyone may answer back. These meetings rest on the operator's brief alone; the German account describes the wandering and the speaking without naming this city. What gathers is the youth movement, or its edges, boys and girls who have already decided that their parents' Germany is unbreathable and are looking for someone who has been living outside it for a decade. He is not their organiser and never becomes one.
suggested_refs: The Württemberg Jugendbewegung circles of 1912-13
sources: de.wikipedia.org, 'Gustav Gräser', for the wandering-agitator years generally

stops.name: Monte Verità, Laban's school and the man in the grotto
stops.date_confidence: attested within the corpus: laban.journey.json records Rudolf von Laban opening his School for Art on Monte Verità in summer 1913 and naming 'the prophet Gusto Gräser in his rock grotto below'; mary_wigman.journey.json and suzanne_perrottet.journey.json both record climbing to the grotto to see him. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from laban.journey.json. Contradiction flagged: de.wikipedia's chronology has Gräser returning to the mountain only until about 1909 and travelling Germany with the wagon from 1911, which sits badly with the corpus's report that he was still in the grotto in 1913.
stops.campa: Rudolf von Laban opens a school for movement on the mountain and begins inventing, on this slope, the notation and the training that modern dance will run on for the next century. He tells his students what else is on the hill: a prophet, in a rock grotto, below the meadow. Mary Wigman climbs down to look at him. So does Suzanne Perrottet. They go, they say, for the spirit of the place. The German chronology has him off this mountain since about 1909 and on the German roads since 1911. The dancers say he was in the grotto. Nobody reconciles the two.
suggested_refs: Rudolf von Laban's Schule für Kunst on Monte Verità, opened summer 1913

stops.name: Hoher Meissner, the Freideutscher Jugendtag
stops.date_confidence: attested. The first Freideutscher Jugendtag met on the Hoher Meissner on 11-12 October 1913, and de.wikipedia, 'Erster Freideutscher Jugendtag' lists Gräser by name among the participants, which upgrades this from operator-brief report to sourced. The coordinate is the summit per de.wikipedia, 'Hoher Meißner'; an earlier working coordinate of 51.3167/9.9167 was about eleven kilometres north, off the massif, and is discarded.
stops.campa: Some two thousand of the German youth movement climb the Hoher Meissner in October to declare that they will shape their lives by their own decision and their own responsibility, before their own conscience. The organisers are professors, publishers and league secretaries. Gräser is on the mountain and on the participant list, and he belongs to none of the committees: he stands at the pacifist and life-reform edge of the thing, with the people who mean the declaration literally. Ten months later most of the young men on that summit are in uniform.
suggested_refs: The Meissner Formula of 12 October 1913
de.wikipedia.org, 'Erster Freideutscher Jugendtag', participant list

segments.name: The Death Cell and the Mountain Again

stops.name: Kronstadt, condemned for refusing the war
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction in its mechanics, well attested in its core [A/R]. de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser' states he was sentenced to death and after three days in the death cell committed to an asylum. The exact judicial route, the tribunal, the charge as filed, the sentence document, was not verified in this pass and no archival record was located; the date 1915 follows the operator brief and the month is set to 01. Any retrospective psychiatric diagnosis of Gräser is explicitly rejected.
stops.campa: The war returns him to the jurisdiction he was born in. In Kronstadt, the town where the judge's son was registered thirty-six years earlier, he refuses military service to the Austro-Hungarian army and a military tribunal sentences him to death for it. He spends three days in the cell reserved for men who are going to be shot. The court records that would say who sat on the tribunal and under which article he was condemned have not been produced by anyone writing about him, including the people most anxious to prove the story true.
suggested_refs: Austro-Hungarian military tribunal records for Kronstadt, 1915, not located in this pass
sources: operator brief [R] on the unverified judicial mechanics

stops.name: Kronstadt, afflicted with confused ideas
stops.date_confidence: attested that the reclassification is the stated reason for moving him from the death cell to an asylum: de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser' gives the phrase 'mit verwirrten Ideen behaftet' with no deeper footnote. Month set to order the segment; no source gives a date. The label is treated here as an administrative act, not a diagnosis, and no retrospective psychiatric reading of Gräser is offered or accepted.
stops.campa: On the fourth day someone writes down that the condemned man is afflicted with confused ideas, and he is taken out of the death cell and put into an asylum instead. The phrase saves his life. It also solves a problem for the army, which had been about to shoot a man for saying he would not kill, and which would then have had a dead pacifist and a story on its hands. Who wrote the phrase, on whose authority, and after examining him for how long, no source says. The committal records have not been produced.
stops.quote_source: The stated official ground for transferring Gräser from the death cell to an asylum, 1915, per de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'
suggested_refs: Committal records of the Kronstadt asylum, 1915, not located in this pass

stops.name: Monte Verità, three years on his brother's land
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'Von 1916 bis 1918 lebte er mit seiner Familie auf dem Landgut seines Bruders auf dem Monte Verità' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Coordinate inherited from the corpus pin. NOT attested and demoted to [R]: renewed contact with Hesse in 1916 and the gift of his poetic Tao Te Ching recreation that autumn. The cited article ties Hesse to 1907 only, and Tao. Das heilende Geheimnis was published posthumously, Wetzlar 1979. Karl Gräser died in Kassel on 28 October 1916, months into this stay.
stops.campa: Released, he comes back to the hill with his family and lives three years on his brother's ground while the war grinds through the countries on every side of Switzerland. Karl dies in Kassel in the October of the first year, married nine days earlier to Jenny Hofmann after fifteen years of refusing the paperwork. His own recreation of the Laozi, made by a man who read it lying on rock rather than in a seminar, is sometimes placed in these years. It was not printed until 1979, twenty-one years after his death.
suggested_refs: Gusto Gräser, Tao. Das heilende Geheimnis (Wetzlar: Büchse der Pandora, 1979; 2nd ed. 2008), published posthumously

stops.name: Monte Verità, the midnight rite at the grotto
stops.date_confidence: attested within the corpus and cross-checked across four files: laban.journey.json, ida_hoffmann.journey.json, mary_wigman.journey.json and suzanne_perrottet.journey.json all carry the same August 1917 all-night performance of Sang an die Sonne with a midnight station at Gräser's rock grotto, at this coordinate. de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser' separately reports a Sonnenfest at the grotto that season with Dada figures present in the Ascona circle, Marcel Janco, Hans Arp, Hugo Ball and Emmy Hennings; that guest list is [R].
stops.campa: Laban and Mary Wigman run a performance across the whole night of the mountain meadow, sunset to daybreak, and call it Sang an die Sonne. At midnight the company comes down the slope to the rock grotto and dances the demon section in front of it. The land above belongs to Hofmann and Oedenkoven, who bought it; the grotto belongs to the man who was put out of the buying. Then the company climbs back up through the dark to be standing on the meadow for the dawn chorus.
suggested_refs: Sang an die Sonne, Monte Verità, August 1917

stops.name: Ascona, Winke zur Genesung unsres Lebens
stops.date_confidence: attested as a work published in Ascona in 1918, poems and aphorisms (operator brief bibliography, matching de.wikipedia's works list); the text itself was not accessible in this pass, only the title. The Ascona town coordinate is approximate. Month set to 01.
stops.campa: In the last year of the war he prints a book in Ascona with a title that offers instructions: Winke zur Genesung unsres Lebens, hints toward the recovery of our life. Poems and aphorisms, a small run, the format he has used since Vienna. Europe at that moment has some nine million dead soldiers in it, and the book offers hints. No copy was located in this pass; the title is all that could be reached, which is the standing condition of nearly everything he published.
stops.quote_source: Gusto Gräser, Winke zur Genesung unsres Lebens (Ascona, 1918), title
suggested_refs: Winke zur Genesung unsres Lebens (Ascona, 1918), text not located in this pass

segments.name: The Revolution He Would Not Arm

stops.name: Munich, nonviolence in the Raterepublik
stops.date_confidence: attested that he preached nonviolence during the Bavarian revolutionary upheaval, was imprisoned, and was expelled after the White victory (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). One source places Silvio Gesell in the same imprisonment; that pairing is single-sourced [R]. Month set to April, the height of the Raterepublik; no source gives a date for his arrest.
stops.campa: Munich in the spring of 1919 is a city where a soviet republic is declared, defended and then destroyed inside five weeks. He is in it, speaking against violence to people who are arming, and he is imprisoned for it, by one account alongside Silvio Gesell, the economist of free money, who was the republic's finance minister for six days. The date of the arrest is nowhere recorded, nor the charge. Then the Freikorps take the city and kill by the hundred, the survivors are sorted, and he is expelled from Bavaria.
suggested_refs: The Bavarian Raterepublik of April 1919 and its suppression

stops.name: Bad Urach, Am grunen Weg
stops.date_confidence: attested that he met Karl Raichle, Theodor Plievier and Gregor Gog at the land commune Am grünen Weg near Bad Urach in 1919, that Plievier took on a wandering-saint persona partly modelled on him, and that Gog went on to found the Vagabundenbewegung (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Month set to order the segment; no source gives one.
stops.campa: At a land commune near Bad Urach called Am grünen Weg he meets three men off the ships of the Kiel mutiny: Karl Raichle, Theodor Plievier, Gregor Gog. They have just tried to overthrow a state by force and failed at it. Plievier comes out of the encounter carrying himself as a Wanderheiliger, a wandering saint, and goes on to write the novels that made him. Gog goes on to organise the vagabonds of Germany into a movement with a congress and a newspaper of its own. Gräser is forty.
stops.quote_source: Name of the land commune near Bad Urach, per de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'
suggested_refs: The Landkommune Am grünen Weg near Bad Urach
Theodor Plievier's later novels, written after the Bad Urach encounter

stops.name: Erfurt, the Neue Schar in Thuringia
stops.date_confidence: attested that Gräser joined Friedrich Muck-Lamberty's Neue Schar at Pentecost 1920 and moved with it through Thuringia, and that Eugen Diederichs exclaimed 'Ganz Thüringen tanzt!' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Per de.wikipedia, 'Friedrich Muck-Lamberty' the Schar set out in May 1920 from Hartenstein in the Erzgebirge, was proclaimed at the Wandervogel Pentecost meeting in Kronach and wandered Thuringia toward the Wartburg, with its largest gathering at Erfurt, over ten thousand people; Erfurt is used here in place of an earlier arbitrary Saalfeld pin. Lamberty organised the troop, NOT Gräser: any account implying otherwise is [R] hagiography.
stops.campa: Friedrich Muck-Lamberty walks a troop of young people out of the Erzgebirge at Pentecost and into Thuringia, singing and dancing through the towns, and Gräser walks with it, forty-one years old and older than all of them. At Erfurt more than ten thousand people come out to meet them. Lamberty organises the Schar; the later legend that hands Gräser its leadership has nothing behind it. What the publisher Eugen Diederichs wrote at the time was three words: Ganz Thüringen tanzt! All Thuringia is dancing.
stops.quote_source: Eugen Diederichs on the Neue Schar's progress through Thuringia, 1920, per de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'
suggested_refs: Friedrich Muck-Lamberty and the Neue Schar, Pentecost 1920
Hermann Hesse, Die Morgenlandfahrt (1932), whose figure of Leo has been read against the Neue Schar's atmosphere, an analogy and not a settled identification

stops.name: Naumburg, the arrest
stops.date_confidence: attested in de.wikipedia, 'Friedrich Muck-Lamberty', which records Gräser living with Muck in Naumburg and being arrested in November 1921. No day is given and none of the sources reached states the charge. Coordinate is Naumburg an der Saale.
stops.campa: The dancing ends the way these things end. By 1921 the Neue Schar has come apart, taking Muck-Lamberty's reputation with it, and Gräser is living with him in Naumburg. In November the police take him again. Nobody writing about him records the charge, which is characteristic: across four German states and two decades he is repeatedly removed by name and rarely by statute. He is forty-two years old and has now been arrested, expelled or condemned in Saxony, Baden, Bavaria, Hungary and Prussia.
suggested_refs: Prussian police files for Naumburg, November 1921, not located in this pass

stops.name: Dresden, Zeichen des Kommenden
stops.date_confidence: attested as two separate works with two separate years, against the operator brief's single date: 'Zeichen des Kommenden. Sieben Steindrucke mit Textblättern. Dresden 1925' and 'Notwendwerk. Zeichnungen und Gedichte. Steindruckmappe. Dresden 1926' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser', works list). Month set to 01. Note he had been expelled from Saxony in 1912; nothing in the sources explains how he came to be printing in Dresden thirteen years later.
stops.campa: In Dresden he makes two portfolios on stone. Zeichen des Kommenden, signs of what is coming, seven lithographs with text sheets, in 1925; Notwendwerk, drawings and poems, in 1926. Lithography suits him: no publisher, no press run to finance, an image and a hand-set text pulled off a slab and given away. This is the form nearly all his authorship takes. Thirteen years earlier the Kingdom of Saxony had put him across its border by order, and no source reached in this pass explains how he came to be working in its capital.
stops.quote_source: Gusto Gräser, Zeichen des Kommenden. Sieben Steindrucke mit Textblättern (Dresden, 1925), title
suggested_refs: Zeichen des Kommenden (Dresden, 1925)
Notwendwerk. Zeichnungen und Gedichte (Dresden, 1926)

stops.name: Munich, der staatsgefahrliche Rumane
stops.date_confidence: attested for the phrase and for the intervention: de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser' supports 'der staatsgefährliche Rumäne Gusto Gräser' and 'den Protest von Thomas Mann und anderen Schriftstellern'. The fuller list of protesting writers, Michael Georg Conrad, Hermann Bahr, Rudolf von Delius, Ludwig Held, Gerhart Hauptmann, comes from the operator brief only and is [R]; it is not presented here as sourced. Month set to 01.
stops.campa: Bavaria moves to expel him from Germany altogether, on paper, as der staatsgefährliche Rumäne Gusto Gräser: the state-endangering Romanian. He was born an Austro-Hungarian subject in a town that became Romanian in 1920 without his moving an inch, and the new passport is what makes him deportable. Thomas Mann and other writers protest, and the expulsion is dropped. Which other writers signed, the circle's tradition names at length and the cited source does not name at all.
stops.quote_source: Wording of the 1926 Bavarian expulsion proceeding against him, per de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'
suggested_refs: The 1926 Bavarian expulsion file and the writers' protest against it
sources: operator brief, for the fuller list of protesting writers [R]

stops.name: Berlin, the Anti-Kriegsmuseum
stops.date_confidence: attested that he moved to Berlin in 1927, worked in connection with Ernst Friedrich's Anti-Kriegsmuseum, and held public conversations at Alexanderplatz (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). Month set to 01; the coordinate is Alexanderplatz, not the museum's own address, which is not given in the source.
stops.campa: Ernst Friedrich's Anti-Kriegsmuseum hangs the photographs the censors kept out of the papers, the faces of men rebuilt by surgeons after the shells, under captions in four languages. Gräser works there. In the afternoons he stands on Alexanderplatz and holds what he still refuses to call lectures, speech as an encounter rather than a delivery, in the loudest square in the city. Twelve years earlier a tribunal in Kronstadt had sentenced him to death for declining to be in the war these photographs are of.
suggested_refs: Ernst Friedrich, Krieg dem Kriege (1924), and his Berlin Anti-Kriegsmuseum, destroyed by the SA in 1933

stops.name: Stuttgart, the Vagabundenkongress on the Killesberg
stops.date_confidence: attested that Gräser spoke at the Vagabundenkongress organised by Gregor Gog (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). de.wikipedia, 'Gregor Gog' places it at Pentecost 1929 on the Killesberg with about six hundred participants who got past police cordons, and this coordinate replaces a generic city-centre pin about 3.5 km to the south-southeast. Pentecost 1929 fell in May; the exact day is set to 01 because the sources reached give the feast rather than the date.
stops.campa: Gregor Gog, the sailor from Bad Urach, calls a congress of vagabonds on the Killesberg above Stuttgart at Pentecost, and about six hundred people get through the police cordons to attend it. Gräser speaks. He has spent thirty years without a house by choice, which is not the same condition as the men in that field: for them the road is what is left after the factory, the war and the pension office are finished with a man. What he said to them is not recorded.
suggested_refs: Gregor Gog's Vagabundenbewegung and its journal Der Kunde
The Pentecost 1929 Vagabundenkongress on the Killesberg, Stuttgart

stops.name: Grunhorst, the donkey cart
stops.date_confidence: attested that he lived at the Grünhorst reform settlement near Berlin with his son-in-law Otto Großöhmig (1909-2005) and distributed writings from a donkey-drawn cart, and that Bucheckern was published in 1930 (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'; operator brief bibliography). The settlement coordinate is approximate, given only as Grünhorst near the Seddinsee. Month set to 01.
stops.campa: His daughter Gertrud's settlement at Grünhorst, out by the Seddinsee, gathers youth-movement people and readers of Ernst Fuhrmann's biosophy, and he lives there with his son-in-law Otto Großöhmig, who is twenty-one. He proposes trading a motor car for a donkey cart, and gets the cart, and goes out with it to hand his printed sheets to whoever will take them. Bucheckern, beechnuts, appears the same year. He is fifty-one, driving a donkey along the lakes east of Berlin.
suggested_refs: Bucheckern (1930)
The Grünhorst reform settlement near the Seddinsee, and its Ernst Fuhrmann connections

stops.name: Grunhorst, the settlement burned
stops.date_confidence: attested that after the Nazi seizure of power his son-in-law Otto Großöhmig was imprisoned in a concentration camp and that Gertrud's Grünhorst settlement was burned in 1936 (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). No month, no account of who set the fire, and no record of Gertrud's own fate afterward was located in this pass. Coordinate approximate as above.
stops.campa: After the seizure of power his son-in-law Otto Großöhmig is taken into a concentration camp. He is twenty-four. In 1936 the settlement burns. The sources that record the burning do not record who lit it, what became of the people living there, or where Gertrud went next; the sentence stands alone in every account, with nothing on either side of it. Gräser is fifty-seven. Whether he was at Grünhorst on the day it burned is one more thing the record does not say.
suggested_refs: Records of the Grünhorst settlement's destruction, 1936, not located in this pass

stops.name: Seddinsee, the houseboat sold
stops.date_confidence: attested: '1940 verkaufte er sein Wohnboot auf dem Seddinsee nahe Grünau und flüchtete nach München' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'), together with repeated arrests through the 1930s and a writing ban around 1940. The coat story, that police gave him a respectable coat which he cut up and remade into his own costume, is [R] legend from the operator brief and is not carried in the prose. Month set to 01; the Seddinsee coordinate is approximate.
stops.campa: By 1940 he is living on a boat on the Seddinsee near Grünau, has been arrested repeatedly through the decade, and is now under a Schreibverbot: not jailed, not deported, forbidden to write. He sells the boat. It is the last property of any kind attached to his name, and he is sixty-one years old. Then he goes south to Munich. How he travelled, what the boat fetched, and who received him at the other end are not recorded in any source reached here.
suggested_refs: The Schreibverbot imposed on Gräser around 1940

stops.name: Munich, the attic rooms
stops.date_confidence: attested that he survived the terror years in Munich 'in den Dachkammern von befreundeten Professoren' (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'). NOT attested and demoted to [R]: the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, absent from that article, and the frequently repeated 1942 start date, since the source gives 1940 for the flight and no start year for the attic period. Near-starvation is reported by the sympathetic tradition. The coordinate is the Munich old-town pin, not any identified address.
stops.campa: In Munich the professors take him in. Not one of the households that hid him is named in any source reached here. Attic rooms, one after another, lent by acquaintances who could be arrested for lending them: this is how the most conspicuous man in the German life-reform movement spends the war, out of sight, in other people's roofs. He had spent forty years standing in public squares where nobody could miss him. The tradition of the people who knew him reports that he was often close to starving.
suggested_refs: The Munich households that sheltered Gräser 1940-1945, unidentified in the sources reached

stops.name: Munich, Siebenmahl and Brieflein Wunderbar
stops.date_confidence: attested that the late manuscript complexes Siebenmahl and Brieflein Wunderbar date from the Munich years (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'); the operator brief adds that Brieflein Wunderbar was addressed to Stuttgart and describes accompanying sound and language investigations, which are [R]. No year is given for either complex by any source reached, and 1950 is set purely to order the segment.
stops.campa: He writes, still, and almost nobody reads it. Siebenmahl and Brieflein Wunderbar, hundreds of pages, along with investigations into sound and word that nobody has published, in a city being rebuilt around him out of its own rubble. Brieflein Wunderbar is addressed, by the tradition that has read it, to Stuttgart: a letter to a city rather than to a person. No source reached gives a year for either complex. He is somewhere past seventy, in a borrowed attic, in handwriting.
suggested_refs: Siebenmahl and Brieflein Wunderbar, in the Gräser estate at the Monacensia, Münchner Stadtbibliothek
sources: operator brief [R] for the addressing and the sound investigations

stops.name: Munich-Freimann, death
stops.date_confidence: attested for date, place, age and circumstance: died 27 October 1958 in Munich-Freimann, 'völlig vereinsamt und unbemerkt', aged seventy-nine (de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser'), though that phrasing comes through Hermann Müller's sympathetic tradition. The pauper's grave is [R]: no cemetery, plot or burial record was located in this pass. The rescue of an unpublished poetry collection 'im letzten Moment vor der Vernichtung aus dem Müll' is Müller's account of his own act [R]. Coordinates for Freimann differ by about 350 m between the sources consulted, 48.1892/11.6106 and 48.1889/11.6153; the first is used.
stops.campa: He dies in Freimann on the northern edge of Munich on 27 October 1958, seventy-nine years old, entirely alone and entirely unremarked, though that phrasing reaches us through the friend who became his editor. By the same tradition he goes into a pauper's grave whose cemetery and plot nobody has since been able to name. Hermann Müller says he pulled an unpublished collection of the poems out of the rubbish at the last moment, and how much of the estate there is nobody reached here says. It sits at the Monacensia in Munich, and at Freudenstein, catalogued.
stops.quote_source: de.wikipedia, 'Gustav Gräser', on the circumstances of his death, 27 October 1958
suggested_refs: The Gräser estate at the Monacensia, Münchner Stadtbibliothek
The Deutsches Monte Verità Archiv Freudenstein
